<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope contains only ordinary metadata assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, dependency arrays, `_commit`, `source`, and a pinned `sha256sums` value. There are no command substitutions, no `eval`, no base64/hex decoding, and no network fetches at source time — the only remote URL is the project's own Gitea archive of a fixed commit.

The `build()` and `package()` functions merely invoke the upstream Python build (`python -m build`, `python -m installer`) and install docs into `$pkgdir`, which is standard packaging and, in any case, does not execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Sourcing this file runs no untrusted code, so the metadata-parse step is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
